To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phenylalanine-glycine motifs function as intracellular cohesion elements that impart structural order to natively unfolded domains of nucleoporin.
the FG motifs of the Nup116 FG domain mediate intramolecular cohesion that imparts order and compactness to its ensemble of structures.
the FG motifs of natively unfolded domains of nucleoporin proteins mediate both intramolecular and intermolecular cohesion of the NPC permeability gate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, dynamics, and function of a family of natively unfolded protein domains that play key roles in the permeability of nuclear pore complexes.
the dynamic structure of the natively unfolded domain of a nucleoporin and its role in the permeability barrier of the nuclear pore complex.
the dynamic structure of a natively unfolded domain from the yeast Nup116 nucleoporin and the role of its phenylalanine-glycine (FG) motifs in mediating intramolecular cohesion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FG motifs of Nups are intrinsically disordered and function as intramolecu- lar cohesion elements to compact the ensemble of structures of FG domains into native premol- ten globular configurations.
the intramolecular cohesion of FG motifs in Nup116 is mediated by a combination of both hydrophobic and hydrogen bonding forces.
phenylalanine-glycine motifs are a key component of the nuclear pore complex and are responsible for the permeability barrier of the nuclear pore.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FG motifs of the nucleoporins are intramolecular cohesion mediators that impart order to natively unfolded FG domains, and this order is required for FG domains to perform their functions at the NPC.
FG motifs are the glue that holds together the NPC diffusion barrier.
the phenylalanine-glycine repeats in FG domains of nucleoporin play a dual role in mediating both intramolecular and intermolecular cohesion in the nuclear pore complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FG motifs in natively unfolded FG domains of nucleoporin proteins are not just random coils, but rather they are intrinsically structured and function as molecular cohesion elements.
the intramolecular cohesion of FG domains mediated by their FG motifs may be a general feature of NPC proteins.
the intramolecular cohesion mediated by the FG motifs of Nup116 is an important factor in determining the dynamic ensemble of its structures and in regulating the permeability of the NPC.
